Hi Jenna / Sam,

Hope you both had a good week. Aurora's annual renewal window is coming up and I wanted to kick off a short planning thread to align on committed capacity for the next 12 months. Your usage over the past year has been steadily increasing (especially for inference-heavy clinical notes summarization and patient triage flows), and we recommend sizing the Dedicated pool to avoid throttles during peak QPS and to lock in a lower unit price.

Quick summary of what I’m proposing:
- Term: 12-month renewal (with option to convert to 24-month at a better rate)
- Target 99th %-ile latency SLO: 120ms for chat endpoint, 40ms for embed/semantic-rerank operations
- Recommended committed GPUs: 16 x A800 (reserved pool) + 4 burst-capable GPUs for sustained peak windows
- Throughput guarantee: baseline 1.8k sustained QPS across the pool, ability to burst to 3.2k QPS for 10-minute windows

I’ve attached a short forecast CSV that includes your observed token throughput and a 12-month growth baseline + conservative and aggressive growth scenarios. Connor and Rishi are looped in for technical sizing and any throughput/latency trade-offs.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Jenna — confirm whether the procurement team prefers a 12- or 24-month term and if there are internal budget windows to align to.
2) Rishi / Connor — can you validate the recommendation above and call out alternate GPU mixes (e.g., more A800s vs. switching to mixed A100/A800) and any operational constraints?
3) Once we align on config, I’ll send through a formal proposal (DocuSign) and the procurement checklist.

Thanks — looking forward to your thoughts.

Hi all — quick sizing note after reviewing the forecast and the observed peak-days in Q3/Q4. I’ll keep the rationale concise.

1) Baseline numbers we used (from the CSV):
- Current 95th %-ile sustained QPS: ~1,100 (observed across chat + rerank endpoints)
- 99th %-ile spikes: up to ~2,700 (multiple short bursts coinciding with business hours and nightly batch inference)
- Average request token length: 420 tokens; median generation length: 140 tokens.

2) Recommended committed pool (primary proposal — balanced latency/cost):
- 16 x A800 (reserved) as primary pool. This provides the best cost/throughput mix for your token profile and maintains our target 99th-% latency SLOs at your projected growth (baseline + 25%).
- 4 x burst A800s (on standby capacity within the same region) to handle sustained short bursts without throttling. Burst capacity billed at a premium but only when used.
- Autoscaling policy: maintain prefix/KV cache for your most common prompts, and route low-latency endpoints to pinned model variants. This improves effective throughput by ~12-18% in real traffic.

3) Lower-cost alternative (if you accept higher tail latency):
- 12 x A800 (reserved) + 2 burst A800s. This cuts committed GPU count by 25% and reduces monthly committed spend by ~22% but raises 99th-% latency risk during the heaviest days — expect tail latency to increase by ~40-70ms on the highest-traffic minutes.

4) Mixed-GPU option (if Aurora prefers hardware diversity):
- 12 x A800 + 4 x A100 (mixed pool) — this slightly increases peak throughput capabilities for large-batch reranks at the cost of higher unit price and more complex scheduling. Not our recommended default unless you have sustained large-batch offline workloads.

5) Throughput guarantees and SLOs:
- For the primary proposal (16+4 burst) we can contract a 1.8k sustained QPS SLA with a 3.2k burst floor for 10-minute windows. Penalty structure and credits can be scoped in procurement; typically a 5% monthly credit for missing sustained throughput targets.

6) Cost estimate (high-level):
- 12-month term: committed monthly spend estimate: $158,000 (primary proposal).
- 24-month term: committed monthly spend estimate: $137,000 (primary proposal) — ~13% lower effective monthly rate.
- Lower-cost alternative (12+2): $123,000/mo (12-month).

7) Implementation notes:
- We recommend a 2-week ramp period with an initial canary rollout: route 20% of production traffic to the new pool for 72 hours, validate latency and KV cache hit rates, then move to full routing.
- We’ll provide a capacity runbook and a JIRA board for rollout tasks; Connor can be the engagement lead for the implementation.

If Jenna/Procurement want, I can convert the cost lines into a redlined quote and include both 12- and 24-month options. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call to walk through the numbers.
